'''Ferox Enclave''' is the restored remains of the [[Carrallanger]] fortress, once part of the [[Zarosian Empire]] before being abandoned and left to decay over the ages. It has since been transformed into a safe haven for travellers by [[Ferox]], a former [[Zamorak]]ian acolyte seeking knowledge to uncover the history of the [[Wilderness]].

The town is a safe area within the Wilderness, meaning players cannot [[Player killing|kill other players]] while within the boundaries of the town. Due to the nature of the [[Tele Block]] spell, Ferox does not allow players who have had it cast on them to enter the town through the town's [[Barrier (Ferox Enclave)|barriers]] until the spell has worn off, though players may still enter whilst in combat. Outside of the town by each entrance, there is a semi-safe-zone area immediately outside the barriers where (under normal circumstances) players cannot be attacked.

While you are tele-blocked, you cannot attack anyone ''by default''. However, anyone within your combat level range ''is able to attack you'' in this "safe" zone. You are able to retaliate against them if this happens. While tele-blocked, someone attacking you will '''not''' prevent them from re-entering Ferox Enclave, provided they are not tele-blocked themselves. Getting a [[skull]] via tele-blocking a player, followed by intentionally dying to get rid of it afterwards, will cause the tele-blocked player ''to gain a skull themselves if they attack you'', as well as being able to attack you "without" retaliation.
<!-- there are also some issues with what exactly is going on with (in terms of reasoning; surely death = not combat tagged / pvp tagged -> opponent will skull, but why is this player able to attack you then?): [teleblocking a player, suiciding, then getting attacked by a teleblocked player in the 'safe' zone will a) not require retaliation and b) will skull the tele-blocked player], but i'm currently unaware of how to precisely test for this. someone smarter than me can fill this in or whatever -->

The town is home to [[Clan Wars]] and [[Last Man Standing]], as well as portals to [[Castle Wars]] and [[Death's Office]]. There is a chapel with an [[altar]] and the [[Pool of Refreshment]] which restores the player's [[hitpoints]], stats, [[prayer points]], and [[Energy|run energy]] (but not [[special attack]] energy).

Players who have paid Ferox {{NoCoins|5000000}} coins can set their [[respawn point]] to Ferox Enclave, by the eastern barrier.

==Transportation==
The level 13 [[Wilderness Obelisk|Wilderness obelisk]] is east of the Enclave. There are also a few safe methods of reaching Ferox Enclave that do not require players to traverse the Wilderness:
* A [[ring of dueling]] will teleport directly here.
* [[Minigame Teleport]] to the [[Bounty Hunter]], [[Last Man Standing]] and [[Clan Wars]] [[minigame]]s.
* Exiting the [[Castle Wars]] area in a free-to-play world.
* Using a [[waka canoe]] along the [[River Lum]] to row here (requires level 57 [[Woodcutting]]).

==Features==
Ferox Enclave is home to refugees and travellers seeking sanctuary in the harsh climate of the Wilderness. As such, followers of various religions appear to tolerate each other's presence within Ferox Enclave; for example, [[Lisa]] and her [[Wizard (Last Man Standing)|wizards]] are [[Guthix]]ian followers, [[Andros Mai]] and [[Sister Scarophia]] are [[Saradomin]]ist followers, and the [[Zamorakian Acolyte|Acolyte]]s are [[Zamorak]]ian followers.

In addition, the aesthetic of the buildings are of various religions as well; the [[Clan Wars]] building contains both Saradomin and Zamorak colours (blue/white and red/black carpets, suits of armour, and flags), the [[Last Man Standing]] contains Guthixian colours (green flames and barriers), while the chapel's altar, dedicated to [[Zaros]], is maintained by Sister Scarophia, a Saradominist.

There are several features found within Ferox Enclave:
* The [[Clan Wars]] and [[Last Man Standing]] [[minigame]]s can be played here.
** The [[Castle Wars portal]] on the eastern side of the Last Man Standing building leads players to [[Castle Wars]].
** The [[free-for-all portal]] on the western side of the Clan Wars building leads players to the free-for-all area of Clan Wars.
* [[Pete Kayer]], who offers several PvP training [[Pete Kayer's Challenges|challenges]]
* A chapel containing an [[altar (Ferox Enclave)|altar]] and [[Pool of Refreshment|Pools of Refreshment]].
* An entrance to [[Death's Office]] can be accessed outside the chapel.
* A pub named [[The Old Nite]], as well as the [[Ferox Enclave Dungeon|caves]] accessed via the pub.
* A [[canoe]] station can be found on the eastern end.
** Adventurers should note that travelling '''to''' the canoe station requires a [[Waka canoe]] while travelling '''from''' the canoe station can be done with any canoe, unless travelling deeper into the Wilderness.
* A [[Ferox Enclave Dungeon|dungeon]] with a portal to [[Soul Wars]] can be found at the north-eastern end.
* A [[Bounty Hunter portal]] leading players to [[Daimon's Crater]] (the player must be on a [[Bounty Hunter]] world).

=== Bank ===
A [[Banker (Ferox Enclave)|banker]] and [[bank chest]] can be found on the western end. The bank is frequently used as a quick bank to a teleport location, in this case for the Ferox Enclave teleport option on the [[ring of dueling]]. The bank is just a few tiles away from the stat and Prayer-restoring amenities, making it a great way for players to quickly restore everything except their [[Special attacks|special attack]] and then re-gear for another trip.

There is also a [[loot chest]], which [[player-killer]]s use to cash in [[loot keys]] from players they killed.

===Exterior===
A few notable features can be found nearby outside of Ferox Enclave.
* Just south of the east entrance is a [[Wilderness Obelisk]] in level 13 Wilderness, which can be used to teleport to any of the other obelisks across the Wilderness.
* An [[altar (Ferox Enclave)|altar]] can be found to the east.
* To the south-east of the Enclave, an unnamed tower with four levels can be found.
** This tower can be used to evade an opponent in [[PvP]] scenarios by climbing up the ladders.
** Additionally, a [[lift Platform (Wilderness)|lift platform]] is located next to the tower's entrance, which can instantly take players to the {{FloorNumber|uk=3}}; however, it is one-way only.

==Personalities==
* [[Ferox]], the founder of Ferox Enclave.
* [[Andros Mai]], a Saradominist warrior seeking to kill [[Vet'ion]].
* [[Banker (Ferox Enclave)|Banker]], a banker assigned to set up a branch in the town.
* [[Camarst]], the barkeep for The Old Nite.
* [[Derse Venator]], a bowman from [[Great Kourend]] seeking to kill [[Callisto]].
* [[Justine]], owner of [[Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing]].
* [[Lisa]], a Guthixian who hosts the [[Last Man Standing]] minigame.
* [[Marten]], a [[canoe]] tutor.
* A [[Mercenary (Ferox Enclave)|mercenary]] hired by the Bank of Gielinor who can perform banknote exchange services.
* [[Perdu]], a dwarven merchant running the [[Lost Property shop]].
* [[Pete Kayer]], who trains players for [[Player killing|PvP]].
* [[Phabelle Bile]], a scientist seeking to obtain a sample of venom from [[Venenatis]].
* [[Refugee]]s seeking sanctuary in Ferox Enclave.
* [[Sigismund]], who is guarding Ferox Enclave.
* [[Skully]], a refugee who allows players to activate the [[Loot key]]s behaviour.
* [[Sister Scarophia]], who maintains the chapel in Ferox Enclave.
* [[Wizard (Last Man Standing)|Wizard]]s, who teleport players to the island where the [[Last Man Standing]] minigame takes place.
* [[Zamorakian Acolyte]]s, seekers of ancient Zamorakian knowledge within the Wilderness.
